soste.title: The Great Mosque gives way to the Cathedral
The Casa de Contratación opens the Americas trade
The Giralda gets its Renaissance belfry
Plaza de España for the 1929 Expo
The river is moved west: Corta de la Cartuja

cards.title: Ferdinand III takes Seville
lines: After fifteen months of siege, the Almohad city surrenders to Castile.

cards.title: The king dies in Seville
lines: Ferdinand III dies in the Alcázar and is buried in the old mosque, now the cathedral.

cards.title: A city of about 50,000
lines: A rough estimate puts the walled city at about 50,000 people.

cards.title: Earthquake
lines: The Giralda's metal spheres fall.

cards.title: Peter's palace
lines: Inscriptions date the palace of Peter in the Alcázar to 1364-1366.

cards.title: A Christian crown
lines: A cross and a bell replace the spheres on the Giralda.

cards.title: Cathedral works begin
lines: In 1401 city leaders decide to replace the great mosque; work starts in 1402.

cards.title: The Inquisition begins here
lines: The first tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition is set up in Seville; the first auto de fe follows in 1481.

cards.title: Gateway to the Americas
lines: The Casa de Contratación makes Seville the port of the Indies.

cards.title: Magellan sets out
lines: Organized in Seville, the fleet leaves Spain on 20 September 1519.

cards.title: A new top for the Giralda
lines: Hernán Ruiz the Younger builds the Renaissance belfry, 1558-1568.

cards.title: The lagoon is drained
lines: An old river branch becomes the Alameda de Hércules.

cards.title: Golden Age Seville
lines: Estimates put the city near 120,000 people.

cards.title: The Great Plague
lines: Estimates of the dead range from a quarter to almost half of the city.

cards.title: A shrinking city
lines: The population is estimated at about 70,000.

cards.title: Trade moves to Cádiz
lines: The Casa de Contratación leaves Seville.

cards.title: Royal Tobacco Factory
lines: Work starts on one of the first large industrial buildings in modern Europe.

cards.title: Lisbon earthquake
lines: The Giralda and the Torre del Oro are damaged; nine people die in Seville.

cards.title: Torre del Oro
lines: Its third level is rebuilt after the earthquake.

cards.title: The Maestranza bullring rises
lines: The inner gateway and the Prince's box go up between 1761 and 1765.
Construction then stops from 1766 to 1784.

cards.title: French occupation
lines: Marshal Victor occupies the city on 1 February 1810.

cards.title: Encarnación convent demolished
lines: The convent comes down during the French occupation.

cards.title: A market square
lines: A market with three covered aisles rises on the Encarnación site.

cards.title: Church property is sold off
lines: The Mendizábal confiscations of 1835-1837 put church property up for sale.

cards.title: 100,498 people
lines: The municipal census counts 100,498 residents.

cards.title: Isabel II Bridge
lines: Work begins in 1845 on the first solid bridge in Seville.
Until then a pontoon bridge of boats, first built by the Moors in the 12th century, crosses the river.

cards.title: Isabel II Bridge opens
lines: The first solid bridge in Seville replaces a pontoon bridge that lasted almost seven centuries.

cards.title: Plaza Nueva
lines: A convent site becomes a square, begun in 1852 and finished in 1856.

cards.title: 112,529 people
lines: The city has grown by 12% since 1842.

cards.title: The walls come down
lines: After the 1868 revolution the walls are partly demolished; the Macarena stretch survives.

cards.title: Finishing the Maestranza
lines: An architect is hired to complete the bullring, unfinished since the 1760s.

cards.title: 133,247 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: 147,271 people
lines: The city is still mostly inside its old circuit.

cards.title: Alfonso XIII Canal
lines: Work starts on the Tablada cut; it resumes in 1919 and ends in 1926.

cards.title: The Guadalquivir floods
lines: The river floods in February 1917.

cards.title: The river will move
lines: A plan turns the old river into a dock and sends the river west of Triana.

cards.title: Ibero-American Exposition
lines: Plaza de España and María Luisa Park open to the world.

cards.title: Spanish Civil War
lines: On 18 July General Queipo de Llano takes Seville for the rebels.

cards.title: 302,300 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: Chapina is plugged
lines: The old river entrance is closed; the city side becomes a dock.

cards.title: Los Remedios
lines: A large planned neighbourhood rises on the west bank.

cards.title: Tamarguillo flood
lines: The Tamarguillo overflows and floods much of the city.

cards.title: Another flood
lines: The Guadalquivir peaks at 6,000 cubic meters per second, the record in Seville.

cards.title: Encarnación market demolished
lines: The square stays empty for decades, used as parking.

cards.title: Spain turns to democracy
lines: Franco dies on 20 November 1975; the Constitution follows in 1978.

cards.title: 645,817 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: Expo bridges rise
lines: Work starts on the Alamillo, Barqueta and Centenario bridges.

cards.title: The plug moves north
lines: For Expo 92 the Chapina plug is reopened and moved to San Jerónimo.

cards.title: Santa Justa station
lines: The new railway station opens on 2 May 1991.

cards.title: Centenario Bridge
lines: A 565 m cable-stayed bridge opens on 15 November 1991.

cards.title: Expo 92 opens
lines: 20 April - 12 October 1992, on La Cartuja.

cards.title: High-speed rail
lines: The Madrid-Seville high-speed line opens in 1992.

cards.title: Isla Mágica
lines: A theme park opens on the old Expo grounds on 28 June 1997.

cards.title: 684,633 people
lines: The city holds steady while the metro area keeps growing until 2007.

cards.title: Metropol Parasol
lines: "Las Setas", a giant wooden canopy, is completed over the Encarnación square.

cards.title: Torre Sevilla
lines: At 180.5 m it becomes Andalusia's tallest building.

cards.title: Seville today
lines: 688,714 people.
